body.heading: Queues concentrate strangers
paragraphs: A queue is a temporary society with one shared frustration. That makes it an efficient place for kindness: everyone is close, everyone is waiting, and a single considerate act is witnessed by twenty people who will shortly be in someone else's queue.

The basics cost nothing: let the person with one item go ahead of your full trolley, wave the parent with the melting-down toddler forward, hold your place patiently instead of sighing at the person counting coins.

body.heading: Kindness is contagious in lines
paragraphs: Watch what happens after one person lets someone through: the whole queue softens. People who have been shown patience pass it on, sometimes within the same five minutes. A queue has a mood, and it is set by whoever acts first.

The reverse is also true, which is the practical argument: one person's irritation gives everyone else permission. Being the first mover in the kind direction is a genuinely useful social skill, and queues are where it is cheapest to practise.

body.heading: When you are the slow one
paragraphs: Everyone is eventually the person at the front apologising. Accept the patience of the people behind you with thanks rather than panic — fumbling helps no one — and remember the feeling next time you are the one waiting. The queue is a rotation; we all take both parts.
Teaching children queue patience is mostly this: narrate it kindly. 'They are doing their best, we will be there soon' is a worldview, absorbed one line at a time.
